subtitle: How a Night Hymn Became Law in Stone, Silk and Body

panels.shot: nighttime wide of Jagannath Temple spire against starlit sky, faint silhouettes of singers and dancers at the sanctum door
panels.action: A Jagannath Sevayat stands at the threshold of the glowing sanctum as a Mahari’s poised silhouette hints at dance, the great temple of Puri rising behind them into the night.

dialogue.text: For centuries in Puri, the Gita Govinda was not just a song. It was temple law, night ritual, sacred dance and woven cloth—until new powers tried to silence its living human voices.

i18n.hi: सदियों तक पूरी में गीत गोविंद सिर्फ़ गाना नहीं था। वही मंदिर का नियम, रात की रीत, पवित्र नृत्य और बुना हुआ कपड़ा था—जब तक नई ताकतों ने इसकी मानवी आवाज़ दबाने की कोशिश नहीं की।

panels.shot: low-angle dawn wide of Jagannath Temple complex with sea in distance
panels.action: The Jagannath Temple towers over the sands of Puri at dawn, its massive vimana catching first light while Sevayats stir in courtyards and a lone Mahari crosses a pillared corridor.

dialogue.text: Under the Eastern Ganga kings, Puri rose as Jagannath’s city. Stone, sea and sandalwood smoke framed a daily cycle of seva in which music and movement were offerings as real as rice or gold.

i18n.hi: पूर्वी गंगा राजाओं के समय, जगन्नाथ की नगरी के रूप में पूरी चमकी। पत्थर, समुद्र और चंदन धुएँ के बीच सेवा का रोज़ का चक्र चलता, जहाँ संगीत और गति चावल या सोने जितनी सच्ची भेंट थे।

panels.shot: intimate interior wide of sanctum doorway at night, Sevayat preparing for Badasinghara
panels.action: Inside the temple at night, a Jagannath Sevayat adjusts lamps and flowers before the dark doorway of the sanctum, other attendants arranging cushions for the reclining deity.

dialogue.text: Among many services, one became the jewel of the night: Badasinghara, when Jagannath reclines to rest. Here, over time, a single poem would rule the sound of the darkness.

i18n.hi: अनेकों सेवाओं में एक रात का नगीना बना: बड़ा सिंघार, जब जगन्नाथ विश्राम को लेटते हैं। यहाँ, समय के साथ, एक ही कविता ने अँधेरे की धुन पर राज किया।

panels.shot: medium shot inside corridor, Sevayat holding palm-leaf manuscript with Gita Govinda verses
panels.action: A Sevayat sits cross-legged beneath an oil lamp, studying a palm-leaf manuscript etched with Sanskrit verses, his lips moving silently as he rehearses the familiar lines.

dialogue.text: From the 12th century onward, Jayadeva’s Gita Govinda spread across eastern India. In Puri, it slowly passed from beloved song to mandated liturgy, its verses scheduled for the god’s nightly hearing.

i18n.hi: बारहवीं सदी से जयदेव का गीत गोविंद पूर्व भारत में फैल गया। पूरी में यह धीरे-धीरे प्यारे गीत से ठहरे हुए विधान बना, इसकी पंक्तियाँ भगवान की रात की सुनवाई के लिए तय हुईं।

panels.shot: wide shot of temple office-like space, Sevayats conferring with palm-leaf Madala Panji
panels.action: Several Sevayats lean over a long low table, one unrolling the temple’s palm-leaf chronicle while another points at inscribed lines, others listening with attentive faces.

dialogue.text: The temple’s Madala Panji—preserved mostly in later copies—records, in its own chronicle tradition, that the Gita Govinda became prescribed. Night seva without its songs was unthinkable in Puri’s memory.

i18n.hi: मंदिर का मडला पंजी—जो ज़्यादातर बाद की प्रतियों में बचा है—अपनी परंपरा में दर्ज करता है कि गीत गोविंद अनिवार्य हो गया। रात की सेवा बिना इसके गीतों के पूरी की याद में अकल्पनीय थी।

panels.shot: dim sanctum threshold, Sevayat singing towards unseen deities, other attendants listening
panels.action: At the sanctum threshold, a Sevayat singer stands with eyes closed and hands folded as his mouth opens in song, while silhouettes of other attendants freeze in reverent stillness.

dialogue.text: By the early modern era, Badasinghara meant the Gita Govinda. Different Sevayat lineages were assigned specific songs. Night after night, they voiced Radha and Krishna’s longing to the wooden lord.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक काल की शुरुआत तक बड़ा सिंघार का मतलब ही गीत गोविंद था। अलग-अलग सेवायत वंशों को ख़ास गीत मिले। रात-दर-रात वे राधा–कृष्ण की तड़प लकड़ी के प्रभु को सुनाते रहे।

panels.shot: wide of temple interior court, Mahari poised to begin dance before inner door
panels.action: A Mahari stands before the inner doorway, ankles adorned with bells, body angled in graceful tribhanga, her focus fixed on the invisible presence within as attendants keep a respectful distance.

dialogue.text: Alongside the voice stood the body. Maharis—hereditary temple dancers and ritual women—embodied the songs in movement. Their dance was not for a public stage, but for Jagannath within.

i18n.hi: आवाज़ के साथ देह भी साथ खड़ी थी। महरी—वंशगत मंदिर नर्तकियाँ और अनुष्ठानिक स्त्रियाँ—इन गीतों को नृत्य में ढालती थीं। उनका नृत्य जन मंच के लिए नहीं, भीतर के जगन्नाथ के लिए था।

panels.shot: medium action shot, Mahari dancing subtle abhinaya to a seated Sevayat singer
panels.action: In a lamplit hall, a Sevayat sings seated at one side while the Mahari dances, eyes expressive, hands shaping Radha’s shyness and Krishna’s appeal, her form echoing the cadence of the verses.

dialogue.text: Frederique Marglin’s research shows Mahari rituals intertwined with temple economy and status. They danced abhinaya to Gita Govinda lines, the poem turned into gesture, gaze, steps and silences.

i18n.hi: फ़्रेडरिक मार्गलिन की खोज दिखाती है कि महरी अनुष्ठान मंदिर की अर्थव्यवस्था और प्रतिष्ठा से गुँथे थे। वे गीत गोविंद की पंक्तियों पर अभिनय नृत्य करतीं—कविता अंग, नज़र, क़दम और विराम बन जाती।

panels.shot: close-up of Mahari’s face mid-dance, intense inward focus
panels.action: A Mahari’s face fills the frame as she holds a delicate mudra near her cheek, eyes lowered yet bright, breath steady, the faint glint of ornaments catching the lamp’s glow.

dialogue.speaker: the_jagannath_sevayats_and_maharis
dialogue.text: He sleeps, but the song must reach him. My body must become its path.

i18n.hi: वह सो रहा है, पर गीत उसे पहुँचना चाहिए। मेरा शरीर ही इसकी राह बनेगा।

panels.shot: workshop interior, weaver at loom creating Khandua cloth with faint script-like patterns
panels.action: In a village weaving room, an Odia weaver bends over a wooden loom, threads of red and cream stretching forward as he carefully inserts patterned bands resembling tiny lettered motifs.

dialogue.text: The same verses travelled into cloth. In Kenduli and nearby weaving centres, Khandua textiles were created with Gita Govinda lines patterned into their borders, offered at Puri as garments for Jagannath.

i18n.hi: यही श्लोक कपड़े में भी चले गए। केंद्रुई और आसपास की बुनाई बस्तियों में खंडुआ वस्त्र बुने गए, जिनकी किनारों में गीत गोविंद की पंक्तियाँ रची होतीं, जगन्नाथ के परिधान बनकर पूरी में चढ़तीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Sevayat presenting Khandua cloth inside temple, Mahari watching
panels.action: A Sevayat carefully unfolds a Khandua cloth before the sanctum door, its motif bands visible, while a Mahari stands to one side, watching the offering with quiet recognition.

dialogue.text: Textile scholars note these Khandua as material liturgy. Here, the Gita Govinda did not only sound or move—it warmed the deity’s wooden limbs, its words fixed in silk and cotton.

i18n.hi: कपड़ा विद्वान इन खंडुआ को मूर्त आरती मानते हैं। यहाँ गीत गोविंद सिर्फ़ गूँजता या नृत्य नहीं करता—यह देवता की लकड़ी की देह को ताप देता है, इसके शब्द रेशम और सूती में थिर रहते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of bustling Puri street, Mahari moving through crowd with dignity
panels.action: On a busy Puri street lined with shops and shrines, a Mahari walks with measured grace, her temple ornaments simple but distinct, some townsfolk greeting her, others whispering from the side.

dialogue.text: Maharis lived within this temple-city web. Marglin traces their complex status—both revered as ritual wives of the god-king and constrained by rules, dependence and the expectations of patrons and priests.

i18n.hi: महरी इस मंदिर–नगरी के जाल के भीतर रहती थीं। मार्गलिन उनकी जटिल स्थिति दिखाती हैं—भगवान-राजा की विधि–पत्नी के रूप में पूजित और साथ ही नियमों, निर्भरता और यजमानों व पुरोहितों की अपेक्षाओं से बँधी हुई।

panels.shot: interior office-like scene during colonial era, British official with papers facing Sevayats
panels.action: In a colonial-period office near the temple, a British official in uniform sits stiffly with files open, while Sevayats stand before him, some anxious, as the official gestures toward a printed regulation.

dialogue.text: Then new rulers arrived. Colonial administrators sought to regulate temple life through law, revenue and ‘reform’. Devadasi systems across India came under moral scrutiny, including Puri’s Maharis.

i18n.hi: फिर नए शासक आए। औपनिवेशिक अफ़सरों ने क़ानून, राजस्व और ‘सुधार’ से मंदिर जीवन को कसने की कोशिश की। पूरे भारत के देवदासी तंत्र सवालों में आए, पूरी की महरी भी।

panels.shot: somber interior, Mahari listening as a local reformer reads from pamphlet
panels.action: In a shaded courtyard, a Mahari sits at the edge while a local reform-minded man reads from a printed pamphlet condemning devadasi practice, a few townspeople nodding, others looking uneasy.

dialogue.text: Across the early 20th century, Indian social reformers and colonial laws converged. Devadasi and Mahari institutions were recast as ‘immoral’, their ritual roles overshadowed by a new language of vice.

i18n.hi: बीसवीं सदी के आरंभ में भारतीय समाज सुधारक और औपनिवेशिक क़ानून एक जगह मिले। देवदासी और महरी संस्थाएँ ‘अनैतिक’ कहकर बदली गईं, उनके अनुष्ठानिक काम पर नए पाप की भाषा छा गई।

panels.shot: medium shot of temple corridor, Mahari’s ornaments removed, simple sari, looking at closed door
panels.action: In a familiar temple corridor now more austere, a Mahari stands in a plain sari, her ceremonial jewellery gone, staring at a door leading nearer to the sanctum that stands firmly closed.

dialogue.text: Legal bans, changing temple administration and rising stigma narrowed their access. Marglin documents how Mahari dance at Puri’s core rituals declined, until little of their night presence remained.

i18n.hi: क़ानूनी पाबंदियाँ, मंदिर प्रशासन में बदलाव और बढ़ते कलंक ने उनकी पहुँच सिकोड़ दी। मार्गलिन बताती हैं कि कैसे पूरी की मुख्य रीतियों में महरी नृत्य घटता गया, जब तक रात में उनकी मौजूदगी लगभग मिट न गई।

panels.shot: wide shot of empty performance space in temple at night, lamps flickering but no dancer
panels.action: At Badasinghara time, the lamplit hall before the sanctum lies empty, lamps flickering against stone, as a distant Sevayat’s song echoes alone without any dancer in the foreground.

dialogue.text: The Gita Govinda continued as sound. Sevayats still sang at night. But the full circle—song, dance, cloth, embodied presence—was torn, its hereditary custodians pushed to the margins or gone.

i18n.hi: गीत गोविंद ध्वनि बनकर चलता रहा। सेवायत अब भी रात में गाते हैं। लेकिन पूरा चक्र—गीत, नृत्य, कपड़ा, सजीव उपस्थिति—टूट गया, इसके वंशगत रखवाले हाशिए पर धकेल दिए गए या खो गए।

panels.shot: close-up of elderly former Mahari at home, holding old anklets
panels.action: In a modest house, an elderly woman identified as a former Mahari sits by a window, turning old ankle bells in her hands, her gaze distant yet steady.

dialogue.speaker: the_jagannath_sevayats_and_maharis
dialogue.text: They remember the song, the poem, the cloth. Will they remember us?

i18n.hi: वे गीत को याद रखेंगे, कविता को, कपड़े को। क्या वे हमें भी याद रखेंगे?

panels.shot: modern-day temple wide, pilgrims thronging, distant view of evening ritual
panels.action: In contemporary Puri, crowds of pilgrims move toward the towering temple as evening falls, while inside, Sevayats prepare for Badasinghara amid electric lights and loudspeakers.

dialogue.text: Today, Puri’s nights still ring with Gita Govinda. Scholars, artists and activists recover Mahari histories, and Khandua weavers keep patterns alive. But the old world of temple dancers survives mostly in memory.

i18n.hi: आज भी पूरी की रातें गीत गोविंद से गूँजती हैं। विद्वान, कलाकार और कार्यकर्ता महरी इतिहास को वापस जोड़ रहे हैं, और खंडुआ बुनकर डिज़ाइन ज़िंदा रखते हैं। पर मंदिर नर्तकियों की पुरानी दुनिया ज़्यादातर यादों में बसती है।

panels.shot: symbolic composite: sanctum glow, shadow of dancing figure, folded Khandua in foreground
panels.action: The frame blends temple space and symbols: the sanctum’s glow in the background, a faint translucent silhouette of a dancing Mahari, and a folded Khandua cloth resting on a stone ledge in the foreground.

dialogue.text: The night song of Jagannath was carried by Sevayats’ voices, Maharis’ bodies and weavers’ threads. A living tradition endures only when these people, and their full dignity, remain part of its story.

i18n.hi: जगन्नाथ का रात का गीत सेवायतों की आवाज़ों, महरियों के शरीरों और बुनकरों के धागों से चला। कोई भी जीवंत परंपरा तभी टिकती है जब ये लोग, और उनकी पूरी इज़्ज़त, उसकी कहानी के भीतर बने रहें।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Night Hymn Became Law in Stone, Silk and Body
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक रात की आरती पत्थर, रेशम और देह में क़ानून बनी
